stories.headline: Train collision in central Spain kills 69 people as safety system investigation begins
stories.body:
A high-speed train collided with a stationary train in central Spain on Wednesday morning [c1]. The crash near Urda killed 69 people [c2]. It also injured more than 100 people [c2]. The moving Renfe AVE train struck the stationary Iryo train from behind at about 8:53am [c1, c16].

Spain began three days of official mourning on Thursday after the crash [c8]. Spanish train drivers went on strike to demand more investment in railway safety [c9]. Foreign ministry officials reported that 42 foreign citizens from seven countries were involved in the accident [c10]. One foreign citizen died [c10]. At least seven foreign citizens suffered injuries [c10].

Rescuers took the bodies of victims to the main forensics institute in Toledo [c3]. Families provided DNA samples to help identify their relatives [c3]. The Guardia Civil set up offices in Madrid, Toledo, Córdoba, and Seville to collect DNA samples [c12]. Relatives reported 64 people missing by Thursday morning [c13].

Several prominent people died in the crash [c4, c5, c7]. Julieta Gallego, a 24-year-old long jumper for the AD Sprint athletics club in Madrid, was killed [c4]. Former employment minister Fátima Báñez, aged 59, also died [c5]. She served under former Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy from 2011 until 2018 [c6]. She was the first female employment minister in Spain [c6]. At the time of her death, Báñez chaired the Spanish Confederation of Business Organizations [c5]. Civil Guard officer José Manuel Chacón, aged 31, died in the crash [c7]. Finance lawyer Antonio Montero Domínguez was also among the dead [c7].

Investigators are examining how the crash happened [c11, c14]. A computer malfunction at 8:30am on Wednesday turned off the LZB train control system [c14]. This failure affected a 69-kilometre stretch of track [c14]. Safety rules require trains to travel at a sight speed under 40 kmph when the system is offline [c17]. But control centre operators at Madrid's Atocha station allegedly told the AVE driver to resume normal speed [c15]. The AVE train travelled about 25 kilometres before hitting the stopped train [c18].

Spanish Transport Minister Óscar Puente said rear-end collisions are highly unlikely [c11]. He suggested that human error under inexplicable circumstances caused the crash [c11]. Vox party leader Santiago Abascal accused the Spanish government of being a criminal organization after the crash [c20]. Spain's high-speed rail network carried 45 million passengers last year [c19].

vocab.meaning: scientific tests used by police to solve crimes or identify bodies

stories.headline: ECB President Christine Lagarde announces early resignation for 2027
stories.body:
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced she will leave her post early [c21]. She will step down on February 7, 2027 [c22]. This date is nine months before the scheduled end of her eight-year term [c22]. Lagarde took office in October 2019 [c23]. She was the first ECB president without formal economics training or central banking experience [c23]. French President Emmanuel Macron thanked Lagarde for her leadership through many crises [c24].

Lagarde announced her resignation at the end of a press conference [c25]. At that meeting, the ECB decided to keep its key deposit rate at 2.5% [c25]. Eurozone inflation rose to 3.8% last month [c26]. That was its highest point since September 2023 [c26]. Lagarde said she is stepping down because she wants freedom of speech to speak about global affairs outside monetary policy [c27].

European Council President António Costa announced that the search for her successor will start right away [c28]. French government bond yields climbed to their highest level in 25 years during a political standoff over next year's budget [c29].

vocab.meaning: an official act of giving up a job or position
a general rise in prices over time

stories.headline: Israeli election ends in deadlock as Netanyahu claims fraud by Arab parties
stories.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed Arab Israeli parties used foreign funding to steal Tuesday's election [c30]. His coalition lost its majority in the vote [c30]. Netanyahu and his allies asked the Shin Bet agency to investigate alleged vote-buying in Palestinian communities [c31]. Qatari government adviser Majed al-Ansari denied that Qatar provided funding to influence the election [c34]. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot accused Netanyahu and his Likud party of running a campaign to delegitimize the results [c32].

Israeli President Isaac Herzog urged political leaders not to tarnish an entire community [c33]. Central Elections Committee head Noam Sohlberg asked Shin Bet to investigate foreign interference claims [c38]. Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh called Likud's fraud accusations a racist blood libel [c39]. Arab Israelis make up about one-fifth of Israel's population [c40].

Final tallies gave Netanyahu's coalition 53 seats and Eisenkot's opposition bloc 48 seats in the 120-member Knesset [c35]. Likud won 27 seats to become the largest party [c41]. Arab party lists Joint List and Ra'am won 19 seats combined [c36]. A governing majority requires at least 61 seats [c37].

vocab.meaning: a temporary alliance of political parties forming a government
to make something seem unlawful or untrue

stories.headline: Pentagon fires top army general Brett Sylvia over leaks of classified data
stories.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia over alleged leaks of classified information [c42]. Sylvia led the J5 directorate of the Joint Chiefs of Staff [c42]. An internal report stated Sylvia admitted to sharing classified details about wars in Iran and Ukraine with two journalists [c43]. He failed multiple polygraph tests during the investigation [c44]. The report noted Sylvia met a journalist at a diner in Virginia to share details about military assistance to Ukraine [c45].

President Donald Trump said Sylvia had big problems and said the government is searching for leakers [c46]. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell confirmed action was taken following an Air Force investigation [c47]. The Pentagon referred the case to the US Department of Justice for criminal investigation [c48]. In July 2026, Hegseth created a task force to prosecute leaks [c49]. A defense official said Sylvia was not a central planner for the Iran war [c50]. CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper directs that war [c50]. Sylvia previously commanded the 101st Airborne Division until May 2025 [c51].

vocab.meaning: official information kept secret for national security

stories.headline: Russian drone strike on Dnipro railway station kills 14 in Ukraine
stories.body:
A Russian drone strike hit the main railway station in Dnipro, Ukraine [c52]. The attack killed at least 14 people [c52]. It also injured at least 14 people, including an 11-year-old boy [c53]. Railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said a passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia was at the platform when the drone struck [c54].

Other Russian strikes hit across Ukraine [c55, c56]. A missile strike on Chernihiv killed two 15-year-old girls and injured 25 people [c55]. A drone attack in Kremenchuk killed three people and injured 28 [c56]. Local authorities declared Friday a day of mourning in Chernihiv and Dnipro [c57]. The mayor of Moscow said 613 Ukrainian drones targeted the Moscow region overnight [c58].

Ukrzaliznytsia reported that nearly 60% of its 521 damaged locomotives were hit during 2026 [c59]. Ukrainian defense firm The Fourth Law makes an autonomous drone that uses onboard AI guidance [c60]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that AI could make independent battlefield decisions as early as next year [c61].

stories.headline: Supreme Court directs banks to compensate victims of digital arrest scams
stories.body:
The Supreme Court of India instructed the central bank to make banks compensate victims of digital arrest scams [c62]. Chief Justice Surya Kant led a bench addressing the Reserve Bank of India [c62, c63]. The court asked the central bank for a list of authorised financial institutions [c63]. Amicus curiae V S Nappinai asked the court to extend liability to telecom companies [c64]. The court also asked WhatsApp about features to automatically disconnect long calls [c65].

Attorney General R. Venkataramani said digital arrest cases dropped by about 50% from last year [c66]. But official data showed over 21,900 complaints involving more than Rs 647 crore in the first eight months of 2026 [c68]. Scammers pose as police on video calls from fake office setups [c73].

In Kozhikode, a woman lost Rs 1.35 crore to scammers impersonating Mumbai Crime Branch officers [c72]. Delhi police arrested two men in October 2026 for running a mule account [c71]. The court gave the central bank until November 30 to submit proposed new rules [c67].

vocab.meaning: to pay money to someone who suffered a loss
pretending to be another person to trick someone

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab causes severe damage and heavy flooding across eastern India
stories.body:
Andhra Pradesh and Odisha suffered severe flooding and heavy damage after Cyclone Arnab struck eastern India [c75, c77, c79]. The storm weakened into a depression over central Chhattisgarh on October 29, 2026 [c74]. Seven people died in Andhra Pradesh as a result of the cyclone [c83].

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu said the storm caused a preliminary loss of Rs 4,600 crore to the state [c77]. Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar estimated at least Rs 500 crore in damage to electricity infrastructure [c75]. Municipal Administration Minister P. Narayana reported damage at 85 locations across 10 municipalities in eight districts [c85]. To help affected farmers, the state government announced compensation of Rs 1,500 for each fallen coconut and oil palm tree [c84].

Health officials in Andhra Pradesh took emergency action before the cyclone hit [c76]. They relocated 3,100 pregnant women to medical facilities [c76]. These precautionary moves led to 367 births at the hospitals [c76].

In neighbouring Odisha, heavy rainfall caused major disruption [c79]. Patrapur in Ganjam district recorded 546 millimetres of rain in 24 hours ending at 8:30am on Thursday [c79]. This was the highest single-day rainfall at a single location in Odisha in 35 years [c79]. The Odisha government planned to airlift 120 people who were stranded by heavy rains and flooding in Ganjam district [c78].

Floodwaters caused severe damage to transport networks across the region [c80, c81]. A 300-metre section of National Highway 326 was completely washed away at Ledabandha in Gajapati district [c80]. Railway operators canceled nine trains and diverted 14 others [c81]. This happened after floodwaters rose past safety levels on bridges in the Ichchapuram-Jhadupudi section [c81].

Weather authorities warned of further potential weather systems [c82]. A new low-pressure area formed over the south Andaman Sea at 5:30am on October 29, 2026 [c82].

vocab.meaning: a weather system with low air pressure that brings rain and wind
done to prevent harm or danger in advance

stories.headline: Supreme Court rebukes ministry over control of corporate law tribunal
stories.body:
The Supreme Court of India criticized the Ministry of Corporate Affairs over its handling of commercial tribunal appointments [c86]. Chief Justice Surya Kant said the National Company Law Tribunal and its appellate tribunal were completely hijacked by the ministry [c86]. Senior advocate Sanjiv Sen told the court that 253 out of 320 regular posts in the tribunal remain vacant [c87].

Senior advocate Meenakshi Arora said the ministry outsourced recruitment of contractual staff to a foreign firm [c88]. Chief Justice Kant directed that staff recruitment must go through official selection commissions instead [c89]. The court ordered tribunal heads to submit infrastructure and staffing plans within four weeks [c90]. Two floors at the principal bench building had to close due to collapsing infrastructure [c91].

The NCLT Bar Association reported that 18 benches were running half-day sittings because of member shortages [c92]. Pending cases reached nearly 30,600 by March 2025 [c94]. Corporate insolvency resolution processes averaged 713 days, far exceeding the 270-day legal limit [c93].

vocab.meaning: a special court set up to settle specific types of legal claims
the state of being unable to pay debts

stories.headline: Piyush Goyal says upcoming US trade deal will safeguard domestic farmers
stories.body:
Union Minister Piyush Goyal said an upcoming trade deal with the United States will protect Indian farmers [c98]. He said that the agreement will fully safeguard domestic agricultural interests [c98]. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said trade negotiations are in their last mile [c102]. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said the two sides are very close to an agreement [c103]. Rubio recently visited Mumbai and Jamnagar during a trip to India [c96].

Bilateral trade between India and the United States reached about $240 billion in 2025 [c95]. Goyal noted that India previously withdrew from RCEP negotiations in Bangkok in November 2019 [c99]. He also said that 60% of India's electricity capacity comes from green sources [c100]. Goyal said the government has concluded eight free trade agreements in total [c101]. A US law passed in 2026 authorised tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian energy [c97].

vocab.meaning: taxes placed by a government on imported goods
